issue_context.title: gh config set browser
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

`gh` requires to open  the default browser at the first time, but it is difficult to open GUI based browser on a SSH terminal.

Add a way to choose a browser that `gh`will launch so that users can use it via SSH terminal.

### Proposed solution

Add `gh config set browser` feature which can set browser path.

### Additional context
comments:
> Add a way to choose a browser that `gh`will launch so that users can use it via SSH terminal.

I agree that it would be useful that people can configure their preferred browser for authentication and for `issue/pr/repo view --web` commands! Note that currently you can select a browser by setting the `BROWSER` environment variable.

However, which browser would you use in a SSH terminal session? Note that both gh and your web browser need to be running on the same machine for the redirect after authentication flow to work.

> However, which browser would you use in a SSH terminal session? Note that both gh and your web browser need to be running on the same machine for the redirect after authentication flow to work.

I assumed to use `w3m`.

I tried `w3m` by setting `BROWSER` environmental variable on a normal Ubuntu terminal.
But it didn't work. `gh` just hanged.

It seems `w3m` is not supported for `GitHub`

## Debugging

I tried the following script for debugging.

```
#!/usr/bin/python3

import os
import sys

with open("/tmp/browser.txt", "w") as fout:
	fout.write(" ".join(sys.argv))

```

`export BROWSER=/home/test/browser.py
`

### content of `/tmp/browser.txt`

`/home/test/browser.py https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=yyyyy&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A33611%2Fcallback&scope=repo&state=xxxxx`

## open the URL

I open the URL with w3m by command line. But it couldn't open the URL.
And I also tried to open `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=yyyyy` with `w3m`.

Then I got the message `GitHub no longer supports this web browser`.

> It seems `w3m` is not supported for `GitHub`

Thank you for sharing your attempts. That's correct. For signing up and authentication, GitHub only supports modern graphical browsers with full JavaScript support.

@mislav 

My true request is to enable setting up `gh` on a SSH terminal without relying on a graphical browser.

@m-tmatma To do that, you can authenticate by running a `gh` command on a machine with a graphical browser, then you can copy over your `~/.config/gh/config.yml` file to the machine where you SSH into.
@m-tmatma Sort of! This is what `gh` prints when it was unable to open a browser app for authentication: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/a7242f4ca3a487432870ed12e5284195e8948433/auth/oauth.go#L69-L71

@mislav

This is the result via SSH terminal on clean-installed Ubuntu 20.04.

```
test@test:~/.config$ gh --version
gh version 0.7.0 (2020-04-22)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.7.0

test@test:~$ gh repo clone cli/cli
Notice: authentication required
Press Enter to open github.com in your browser...
Error: no DISPLAY environment variable specified
```

`gh` hangs after `Error: no DISPLAY environment variable specified` via SSH terminal.

```
test@test:~$ gh --version
gh version 0.8.0-pre.2 (2020-05-08)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.8.0-pre.2
test@test:~$ gh repo clone cli/cli
Notice: authentication required
Press Enter to open github.com in your browser...
Error: no DISPLAY environment variable specified

```

> @m-tmatma To do that, you can authenticate by running a `gh` command on a machine with a graphical browser, then you can copy over your `~/.config/gh/config.yml` file to the machine where you SSH into.

If you want to skip the requirement for a browser, `gh` expects the mentioned file to have the following contents:

```yaml
hosts:
    github.com:
        oauth_token: <github auth token>
        user: <user id>
```

I copied config.yml which is created on Windows. 
But gh asked me to press enter to open browser.

```
test@test:~$ gh repo clone cli/cli
Notice: additional authorization required
Press Enter to open github.com in your browser... 
```

I used 0.8.0 on windows and ubuntu.

I have the same issue on a headless Ubuntu 18.4.4 LTS even after I copy the credentials from a gui system.

~/.config/gh/ files 
```
$ cat config.yml
hosts:
    github.com:
        oauth_token: 00000000feed0000baba0000beef0000deadbeef
        user: cds-amal

$ cat state.yml
checked_for_update_at: 2020-05-22T00:40:56.988845845Z
latest_release:
    version: v0.8.0
    url: https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.8.0

```

@m-tmatma @cds-amal I don't know why gh insists on authenticating you if you already copied the config file into the right destination (`$HOME/.config/gh/config.yml`), sorry. According to our logic, if that file exists and contains authentication info, you should never be prompted for authentication in the browser. Please check your file paths again, or if you have time, you can get our project code, sprinkle in some debugging statements, and build the project to see what's going on.

@m-tmatma @mislav This seems to be related to a new PERMS requirement on GH

```
 read:org Read org and team membership, read org projects
```

**Workaround**

  1. on gui box: upgrade to ***latest*** version of `gh-cli`
  1. copy over ~/.config/gh/config.yml to its proper location on headless box

My gui-box was two versions behind headless. This should probably noted somewhere. 

**Debugging notes**

My gui was 2 gh-cli versions behind and I copied those credentials to my headless box. It looked like when headless gh-cli detected the credentials were lacking it started the OAUTH browser authorization process which can't be fulfilled on headless. This forced a CTRL-C SIGINT/SIGKILL terminated the process without flushing stdout/err. 

`gh pr list 2>1& > foo` can be used to peek at the data

> @mislav Is that method documented?

Not very well.  So if you're looking for the simple way to open `gh` in your default Windows browser, simply do this:

```
export GH_BROWSER=explorer.exe  # only for gh
```
or globally (other cli tools included)
```
export BROWSER=explorer.exe
```
For logging in via SSH, simply `GH_BROWSER=true gh auth login` and visit https://github.com/login/device in a GUI browser on your local machine. The `true` refers to /usr/bin/true, which is a noop.
